more.question: N5
more.good_when: Every case that the package's own names promise to a caller has its own test named for it, so that a maintainer whose test fails knows which promise broke. Today four promises have none: a credit line whose amount reaches -1000000000 is refused, as the docstring of parse_lines says (the positive end has test_refuses_an_amount_at_the_limit, the negative end has nothing); a Line made with only a description and a price counts as one item; render prints an invoice in a currency other than EUR when it is given one; and subtotal gives 0 for an invoice with no line, as its docstring says.

more.question: N7
more.good_when: Breaking any behavior that the package offers makes a test fail. Today three changes leave all 62 tests passing: dropping the check on the size of a negative amount, so that a credit line of 500000000.00 at quantity -2 is printed instead of refused; changing the quantity that a Line gets when none is given; and changing how a Line shows itself in a traceback or the console (Line.__repr__, lines.py line 36, is the one line that no test runs). A maintainer who breaks any of these sees a test fail.
